items.title: Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Post-Stroke Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With Subgroup Analyses of Standard and Adapted Approaches.

ai.headline: CBT may reduce depressive symptoms after stroke, but results vary widely between studies.
ai.summary: Researchers combined 11 randomised trials involving 994 people with post-stroke depressive symptoms. CBT was linked to a significant reduction in symptoms compared with control conditions, though results were highly inconsistent across studies. Adapted CBT showed a significant effect, while standard CBT did not, but there was no clear difference between the two approaches.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that talking therapies could support emotional recovery after stroke, which matters because depression can slow rehabilitation and affect long-term health.
ai.life_skill: If you or someone you know is feeling low after a stroke, speak to a healthcare professional about whether talking therapy might help.
ai.fact: Depression is a common complication after stroke and can reduce participation in rehabilitation.

quiz.question: Did standard CBT show a statistically significant reduction in post-stroke depressive symptoms in this review?
quiz.answer: No, the pooled effect of standard CBT did not reach statistical significance.

ai.caveat: The studies were highly inconsistent, so the findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Dispelling the fog of pain: evidence and potential mechanisms of traditional mind–body practices for chronic pain-related cognitive impairment—a review on brain fog and executive function

ai.headline: Tai Chi, yoga and qigong may help chronic pain-related brain fog, but proof is still limited.
ai.summary: The review looked at traditional mind-body practices—Tai Chi, yoga and qigong—for people with chronic pain and thinking problems such as poor attention, memory and processing speed. It found only two small direct trials, with mixed results, and no clear proof that these practices improve objective cognitive function. Indirect benefits through pain relief, sleep and mood are possible but should not be read as proof of cognitive improvement.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that popular mind-body exercises are promising but not yet proven treatments for the thinking difficulties that often come with chronic pain.
ai.life_skill: Try a gentle mind-body practice such as Tai Chi, yoga or qigong alongside, not instead of, care from a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Chronic pain is often linked with measurable difficulties in attention, memory, processing speed and executive function.

quiz.question: What does the review conclude about Tai Chi, yoga and qigong for objective cognitive dysfunction in chronic pain?
quiz.answer: They should be regarded as promising adjunctive practices rather than established treatments.

ai.caveat: It is a narrative review with direct evidence limited to two small trials, so it cannot prove that these practices improve thinking skills.

ai.headline: Exergames may not reliably improve cognition in adults aged 50 and over once publication bias is accounted for.
ai.summary: The study combined 48 studies involving 2,605 adults aged 50 and older to see if exergames—video games that combine physical activity with mental tasks—improve cognition. Before adjusting for publication bias, there was a small positive effect, but after adjustment the overall effect was inconclusive and no single cognitive domain showed more than anecdotal evidence of benefit.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that popular brain-and-body games are not yet proven to protect thinking skills in midlife and older age, so people should not rely on them as a proven way to prevent cognitive decline.

quiz.answer: The evidence for an overall effect was inconclusive, and no cognitive domain showed more than anecdotal evidence of benefit.

ai.headline: More university spending per student is linked to higher tax revenue years later, but only if spending per student rises.
ai.summary: The study looked at 121 countries over nearly 40 years to see if government spending on universities pays for itself through taxes. It found that increases in per-student spending are linked to higher direct income and total tax revenue after five to ten years, while simply expanding the university budget without protecting spending per student shows no return.

quiz.answer: Spending per student must increase; expanding the university budget without protecting spending per student yields no return.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and observational data cannot prove that spending caused the tax changes.

items.title: School environment plays key role in shaping parents' educational hopes for their children, suggests study

ai.headline: The school a child attends is closely linked to parents' hopes for how far their child will go in education, especially where segregation is high.

ai.why_it_matters: It shows that the school environment can shape what parents believe their children can achieve in education.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your child's school environment might be shaping your hopes for their education.
ai.fact: Where segregation is high, the school a child attends is closely linked to parents' expectations for their child's years of education.

quiz.answer: Where segregation is high, the school a child attends is closely linked to how many years of education parents expect their child to complete.

ai.summary: Jojo, a gorilla, was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend. It's a complex process.

items.title: Dietary Intake, Diet Quality, and Mealtime Experiences of Community-Dwelling Older Adults in The Netherlands: A Systematic Review.

ai.headline: Older adults living independently in the Netherlands often eat too little protein and vitamin D, with mixed diet quality.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at studies of community-dwelling adults aged 65 and over in the Netherlands. It found that many had protein intakes below recommendations, low dietary vitamin D, and frequently suboptimal intake of fish, dairy and meat alternatives, while fruit intake was relatively adequate and overall diet quality was reasonable but suboptimal. Qualitative findings suggested ingrained habits, limited awareness of protein needs and reluctance to change.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that everyday eating habits among older adults may fall short of nutrition needs, which can affect independence and health in later life.
ai.life_skill: Check whether your meals regularly include protein-rich foods such as fish, dairy, meat or alternatives.
ai.fact: Many community-dwelling older adults in the Netherlands have protein intakes below recommendations and low dietary vitamin D intake.

quiz.question: What did the review find about protein intake among older adults in the Netherlands?
quiz.answer: A substantial proportion had protein intakes below recommendations.

ai.caveat: The review is based on limited studies, some with small or non-representative samples, and few included adults aged 80 and over.

items.title: VIRTUAL SOCIETY AND HEALTH IN THE DIGITAL ERA: OPPORTUNITIES, RISKS, AND STRATEGIES FOR DIGITAL HEALTH LITERACY

ai.headline: Online health communities can help, but digital health literacy is needed to judge sources and avoid misinformation.
ai.summary: This narrative review looked at virtual society, digital health literacy, and institutional responses in Indonesia, drawing mainly on literature and official sources from 2021 to August 2026. It found that online communities may improve support and patient activation, but evidence for lasting behavior change and clinical results is less consistent. The authors propose five linked institutional functions: credibility, participation, literacy, governance, and evaluation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why being able to judge online health information matters for everyday decisions about your own and others’ wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Check who produced a health website or post and whether it is clearly dated before trusting its advice.
ai.fact: Digital health literacy includes appraising sources, interpreting uncertainty, privacy awareness, and knowing when to seek professional referral.

quiz.question: What does the review say about evidence for online communities improving lasting behavior change and clinical outcomes?
quiz.answer: The evidence is less consistent than the evidence that online communities may improve support and patient activation.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review, not a systematic review or randomised trial, so its conclusions are not proof.

items.title: Physical Activity, Exercise-Related Measures and Multimorbidity: A Narrative Review
items.venue: Journal of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences

ai.headline: Being more active is linked to lower death risk in adults with multiple long-term conditions, but other benefits are unclear.
ai.summary: The review looked at physical activity and structured exercise in adults with two or more chronic conditions. Higher activity was linked to lower mortality and longer modelled life expectancy, while effects on getting more conditions, physical and mental function were mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that staying active may help people with several health conditions live longer, but the best types and amounts of exercise are still uncertain.
ai.life_skill: Try building regular movement into your week and discuss a safe activity plan with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Multimorbidity means having two or more chronic conditions at the same time.

quiz.question: What was the clearest finding linking physical activity to health in adults with multiple conditions?
quiz.answer: Higher physical activity was associated with lower mortality and longer modelled life expectancy.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review of mostly observational studies, so it cannot prove that activity causes longer life.

items.title: Trauma Processing Therapy: A Precision-Weighted Approach to Memory Reconsolidation

ai.headline: A new therapy theory proposes updating traumatic memories through precise prediction errors while they are pliable.
ai.summary: The paper introduces Trauma Processing Therapy (TPT), a theoretical approach based on predictive processing. It suggests traumatic memories act as highly precise models resistant to change, and that lasting change requires precisely calibrated prediction error while the memory is in a pliable state.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a new way of thinking about why trauma symptoms may return and how therapy might be improved.
ai.life_skill: Notice when a strong emotional memory feels stuck and consider speaking with a qualified therapist about evidence-based options.
ai.fact: Trauma-focused therapy can help PTSD, but many people do not achieve total remission and symptoms may recur.

quiz.question: What does the paper say about the evidence for TPT?
quiz.answer: It is not evidence for the effectiveness of TPT or for reconsolidation being achieved.

ai.caveat: TPT is a preprint theoretical proposal that has not been empirically tested or peer reviewed.

items.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents

ai.headline: Choosing AI trading personas to match each stock beats using the same team for every stock.
ai.summary: The study tested FinPanel, an AI multi-agent trading system where a recruiter picks a panel of trader personas for each stock based on how that stock trades. Over one year across eight US stocks, the selected panel outperformed a fixed panel and other AI trading agents, and avoided large losses compared with simply buying and holding.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that matching the right people—or AI agents—to a specific task can matter more than how they work together, which applies to teamwork and decision-making in everyday life.
ai.life_skill: Try choosing who works with you based on the specific task you face, rather than using the same group for everything.
ai.fact: Task-conditioned persona selection means picking team members based on the characteristics of the task they will face.

quiz.question: What did the selected panel do compared with a fixed panel of the same size?
quiz.answer: The selected panel was ahead of the fixed panel of the same size.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the results come from a simulated trading environment rather than real-world trading with actual money.

items.title: Fostering campus sustainability: green curriculum, institutional support, and psychological pathways to students’ pro-environmental behavior

ai.headline: Green curriculum and belief in your own ability are linked to students acting more sustainably.
ai.summary: A survey of 282 Ghanaian undergraduates looked at green curriculum, institutional support, environmental attitude, self-efficacy and pro-environmental behavior. Green curriculum, environmental attitude and self-efficacy were positively linked to reported pro-environmental behavior, while institutional support showed no direct link.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that feeling capable may matter as much as what you are taught when it comes to everyday sustainable actions.
ai.life_skill: Notice what makes you feel capable of doing something sustainable, and build on that confidence.
ai.fact: Self-efficacy showed the largest direct association with pro-environmental behavior among the predictors studied.

quiz.question: Which factor showed the strongest direct link to students’ pro-environmental behavior?
quiz.answer: Self-efficacy demonstrated the largest standardized direct coefficient among the predictors.

ai.caveat: A single cross-sectional survey cannot show cause and effect, and the results come from one university in Ghana.

items.title: No convergence in three decades: national trajectories of episode-fatality ratios for childhood lower respiratory infections in 204 countries, 1990-2023

ai.headline: Countries have not converged on better child survival from lung infections over 33 years.
ai.summary: Researchers compared each country’s child lung-infection death rate against the best-performing countries in its region from 1990 to 2023. The typical country made no net progress toward that regional frontier, and the share more than twice as far behind barely changed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that survival once a child falls ill is not automatically improving everywhere, so health-system quality gaps can persist for decades.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether local health services are improving over time and ask qualified health professionals about children’s lung-infection care if concerned.
ai.fact: Lower respiratory infections remain the leading infectious cause of death in children.

quiz.question: Did the typical country narrow its gap to the best regional survival performance between 1990 and 2023?
quiz.answer: No, the median gap showed no net narrowing over the 33 years.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and uses modelled estimates with interpolated data, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Preconception Medicaid and Maternal and Infant Health: Evidence from Linked Administrative Data -- by Genna Campain, Sarah Miller, Petra Persson, Maya Rossin-Slater, Laura Wherry, Katlyn N. King

ai.headline: Getting Medicaid before pregnancy improved care and screening but did not improve mothers' or babies' health.
ai.summary: Researchers studied first-time mothers in California around the 2014 Medicaid expansion to see if insurance before pregnancy helped. Coverage, prenatal care and STI screening increased, but mothers' and infants' health did not improve. The authors conclude that preconception coverage alone may not close health gaps.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that simply having health insurance before pregnancy may not be enough to improve health outcomes for low-income families.
ai.fact: Preconception Medicaid coverage increased prenatal care and STI screening but did not improve maternal or infant health in this study.

quiz.question: Did mothers who gained Medicaid before pregnancy have better health outcomes?
quiz.answer: No, the study found no improvements in maternal or infant health despite more coverage and screening.

ai.caveat: This is a single preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so the results are preliminary.

items.title: Spatiospectral signatures of stomach-brain synchrony

ai.headline: The stomach’s natural rhythm may act as a stable scaffold that helps coordinate brain activity across regions and frequencies.
ai.summary: Researchers used MEG and electrogastrography to map how the stomach’s slow rhythm couples with spontaneous brain waves at rest. They found widespread phase-amplitude coupling across delta, theta, alpha and beta bands, distinct spatiospectral fingerprints overlapping a known gastric brain network, and a preferred gastric phase during transitions between stomach waves that was stable across regions, frequencies, connections and time.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a basic bodily rhythm may help organise large-scale brain dynamics, broadening how we understand the brain-body connection.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your body feels when you are resting, as a simple way to stay aware of the brain-body connection.
ai.fact: The human stomach has an intrinsic rhythm of about 0.05 Hz.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find about the timing of stomach-brain modulation?
quiz.answer: There was a consistent preferred gastric phase during the transition between stomach waves, stable across brain regions, frequencies, connections and time.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are preliminary and not yet confirmed.

items.title: Breastfeeding is associated with fewer maternal depressive symptoms, study finds

ai.headline: Breastfeeding is linked to fewer depressive symptoms in mothers in some low- and middle-income countries.
ai.summary: Researchers from the University of Sharjah looked at mothers in selected low- and middle-income countries across Africa and South Asia. They found that breastfeeding was associated with fewer maternal depressive symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests breastfeeding may be connected to mothers’ mental wellbeing in these settings, though it does not prove cause and effect.
ai.life_skill: Notice how feeding choices and mood relate for you, and speak with a qualified health professional if you feel low.
ai.fact: Breastfeeding is associated with fewer maternal depressive symptoms in selected low- and middle-income countries across Africa and South Asia.

quiz.question: What did researchers find about breastfeeding and mothers’ depressive symptoms?
quiz.answer: Breastfeeding was associated with fewer maternal depressive symptoms.

ai.caveat: This is a news report of a single observational study, so it cannot show that breastfeeding causes fewer depressive symptoms.

items.title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study

ai.headline: An osteoporosis drug stopped harmful mineral buildup in zebrafish spines.
ai.summary: Researchers studied spinal degeneration in zebrafish and found a genetic link to the condition. An existing osteoporosis drug prevented damaging mineral buildup in their spines. The findings may lead to future treatments for chronic back pain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how genetic research and existing drugs might one day help prevent or slow spinal degeneration linked to back pain.
ai.fact: An existing osteoporosis drug prevented damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines.

quiz.question: What did the osteoporosis drug do in the zebrafish study?
quiz.answer: It prevented damaging mineral buildup in their spines.

ai.caveat: The results come from zebrafish, not humans, so they do not prove the drug would work in people.

items.title: Foster care placement of American Indian and Alaska Native children falls short of federal legislation aims

ai.headline: Many places are not following federal rules that prioritise placing Native children with relatives or Native families.
ai.summary: The study looked at how American Indian and Alaska Native children are placed in foster care. It found that many jurisdictions have not met the placement guidelines set out in the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows whether a law designed to keep Native children connected to their families and cultures is actually being followed.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether laws intended to protect families are being applied in your community.
ai.fact: The Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978 requires states to first seek to place AIAN children with a family member, a member of the child's tribal nation, or another Native family.

quiz.question: What does the Indian Child Welfare Act require states to do first when placing an AIAN child in foster care?
quiz.answer: The state must first seek to place the child with a family member, a member of the child's tribal nation, or another Native family.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a study, not the full research paper, so details about how the study was done are not available.

items.title: Factors Associated With Burnout in Psychiatric Nurses: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

ai.headline: Burnout in psychiatric nurses is linked to job stress, violence, and low resilience or compassion satisfaction.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis combined 22 studies with 4,735 psychiatric nurses to look at factors linked to burnout. It found burnout was linked to higher job stress, secondary traumatic stress, and workplace violence, and to lower compassion satisfaction, emotional intelligence, and psychological resilience; day shifts were linked to lower burnout.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows which workplace and personal factors tend to go together with burnout, helping people understand what to watch for in stressful jobs.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your workplace offers support for stress, safety, and emotional resilience, and consider asking about it if you feel overwhelmed.
ai.fact: Burnout among psychiatric nurses is associated with multiple psychological and occupational factors, but the evidence does not prove what causes it.

quiz.question: Which factor was positively associated with burnout among psychiatric nurses?
quiz.answer: Job stress, secondary traumatic stress, and workplace violence were positively associated with burnout.

ai.caveat: Most of the included studies were observational, so the review shows links rather than proving causes, and there was substantial variation between studies.

items.title: Investigating the Formation Process of Quiet Quitting in Public Sector Organizations

ai.headline: Quiet quitting in public sector jobs is linked to unfair treatment, poor leadership, few growth chances and heavy workloads.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 17 employees and managers in government organisations to understand quiet quitting. They found it arises from a mix of organisational injustice, leadership style, limited career growth, workload, culture and bureaucracy, leading employees to do the bare minimum and causing burnout and lower productivity.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace conditions can quietly drain motivation and affect both workers and organisations.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you are doing only the bare minimum at work and consider what workplace factors might be driving it.
ai.fact: Quiet quitting means staying in a job while limiting effort to the minimum required duties.

quiz.question: What did the study find quiet quitting leads to?
quiz.answer: It leads to decreased job satisfaction, burnout and diminished organisational productivity.

ai.caveat: This is a small interview-based study, so its findings cannot be generalised or taken as proof of cause and effect.

items.title: LEARNING BUT NOT PROGRESSING
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

ai.headline: More children in Africa are in school, but many are not learning basic reading and maths.
ai.summary: The report looks at education quality across Africa. It finds that higher enrolment and completion rates do not always mean children are gaining foundational skills in reading, mathematics and comprehension.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that going to school is not the same as actually learning, which affects future opportunities and independence.
ai.life_skill: Check whether you can actually use and explain what you have been taught, not just whether you have finished the course.
ai.fact: School enrolment and completion do not guarantee that children acquire foundational reading, mathematics and comprehension skills.

quiz.question: Does higher school enrolment in Africa necessarily mean children are learning foundational skills?
quiz.answer: No, the report finds that enrolment and completion do not necessarily mean children are acquiring expected levels of reading, mathematics and comprehension.

ai.caveat: The report draws on published research, assessments and institutional reports rather than presenting a single new experiment, so it summarises existing evidence rather than proving a new effect.

items.title: Measuring Cognitive Demands in Professional Esports

ai.headline: A new framework uses esports match data to measure seven types of mental demand during play.
ai.summary: Researchers studied records from 314 professional DOTA 2 matches involving 558 player accounts and about 2,184 player-hours. They developed TRACE, which measures four player-level and three team-level cognitive demands, such as task switching and decision-making under uncertainty. The framework turns match replays into large-scale data for studying how often people face different mental demands and how they respond.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday digital activities can be used to study real-world thinking skills outside the lab.
ai.life_skill: Notice which mental tasks come up most often in a game or activity you do regularly.
ai.fact: TRACE measures seven dimensions of cognitive demand, including cognitive control capacity, task switching, inhibitory control, dynamic attention, visuospatial working memory and updating, decision-making under uncertainty, and feedback learning.

quiz.question: What does TRACE turn match replays into?
quiz.answer: A source of large-scale behavioral data for cognitive psychology.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it is based on one video game rather than proof that esports improves thinking skills.

items.title: Mapping NGFS Climate Pathways to GICS Sectors: Application to Portfolio Decarbonization

ai.headline: A new way to map climate scenarios to investment sectors to track portfolio emissions.
ai.summary: The study matches climate scenario sectors to investment sectors based on greenhouse gas emissions rather than names. It then scales global climate pathways down to individual portfolio sectors, adjusting for where companies operate. Applied to two example ETFs, it shows how sector mix and regional paths affect financed emissions.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people understand how investment portfolios are measured against climate goals and what drives their financed emissions.
ai.life_skill: Check how your investments are classified by sector and region before assuming they align with climate targets.
ai.fact: Scope 1 and 2 emissions are direct emissions from a company and from the energy it buys.

quiz.question: What did the researchers use to match climate sectors to investment sectors?
quiz.answer: They used the materiality of Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions rather than semantic similarity.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and was applied only to two illustrative ETF indices.

items.title: The relationship between school support and teachers' perceived AI teaching application competence: the mediating roles of psychological and cognitive factors and the moderating role of practical experience

ai.headline: School support helps teachers feel more able to use AI in class, mainly through confidence and skills rather than directly.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 782 primary and secondary school teachers about perceived school support and their own AI teaching application competence. They found school support was not directly linked to competence, but was linked indirectly through psychological resilience, AI anxiety, self-efficacy and AI-TPACK. Practical experience was positively linked to competence and strengthened the links of AI-TPACK and self-efficacy with competence.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that feeling supported at school may build teachers’ confidence and reduce anxiety about using AI, which matters as AI becomes more common in classrooms.
ai.life_skill: Notice what support your school or college offers for new digital tools and use it to build your confidence.
ai.fact: Perceived school support was indirectly associated with teachers’ perceived AI teaching application competence through psychological resilience, AI anxiety, self-efficacy and AI-TPACK.

quiz.question: Was the direct link between perceived school support and teachers’ AI teaching competence statistically significant?
quiz.answer: No, the direct association was not statistically significant; the significant links were indirect through other factors.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional survey, so it cannot show that school support causes changes in teachers’ AI teaching competence.

items.title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories

ai.headline: An AI system can spot lab quality problems days before staff act, but it is only a preprint.
ai.summary: Researchers built LabARIA, a multi-agent AI system that watches lab workflows, quality control, and operations together. In one hospital’s data, it flagged most quality-control actions before they happened, with a median lead time of 5.4 days, and helped predict staffing and inventory risks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI might help hospitals catch laboratory errors earlier, which could support safer patient care in the future.

quiz.question: What did LabARIA do before most recorded lab quality-control actions?
quiz.answer: It generated warnings before 407 of 422 recorded QC actions, with a median lead time of 5.4 days.

ai.caveat: This is a single-center retrospective preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so it cannot yet prove the system improves real-world decisions or patient care.

items.title: Horizontal Equity of Taxation: Citizen Beliefs and Policy Preferences -- by Pierre Bachas, Christopher A. Hoy, Anders Jensen, Mahvish Shaukat

ai.headline: People notice unfair taxes on self-employed workers, but learning about it does not make them want to fix it.
ai.summary: Researchers looked at tax data from 29 developing countries and found that self-employed people often pay less tax than wage earners with similar incomes. Surveys and experiments in Pakistan showed that telling people about this unfairness made them more concerned, but did not increase support for changing the tax system.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that even when people recognise a tax system is unfair, they may not back reforms to make it fairer.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether taxes treat people with similar incomes differently before forming an opinion on tax reform.
ai.fact: Taxes are often harder to enforce on self-employed workers than on wage earners, creating horizontal inequities among taxpayers with similar incomes.

quiz.question: What happened in Pakistan when people were given information about tax unfairness?
quiz.answer: It raised fairness concerns but did not increase support for reforms to reduce the inequity.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the survey evidence comes from Pakistan rather than all 29 countries studied.
